title: Advice on overwatch and ambush UI in turn based game.
author: Kingfish344
selftext:
Apparently huge mistake posting this anywhere other than here. People seem to be crazy anti AI out here. 

Hopefully, I can get more than what a bunch of AI slop here.

comments.author: warpedspoon
comments.body: I saw some of the other posts and I think the comments actually have a good point in that the menu art looks nothing like the gameplay, AI generated or not.

replies.author: Kingfish344
replies.body: Yeah, menu art was written before any gameplay was built. I thought the menu art looked kind of cool, but probably need to rethink it for sure. All my art is currently AI generated which seems to be a very unpopular decision even though I am unclear why everyone cares so much about that.

comments.author: caster
comments.body:
So right away, probably best to avoid actual tile collisions when being ambushed. A unit moving from a tile on the left into an occupied tile should probably stop where it is, rather than enter the occupied tile and then be displaced unpredictably into a tile on the other side of the unit. This avoids unpredictable movement which could have a lot of follow-on consequences.

If it is your intention to have Overwatch as a mechanic that can interrupt movement, it is probably a good idea to visually show tile-by-tile movement rather than immediately resolve the entire move.

Preview isn't good enough in this case because information is imperfect. A unit may (accurately) show a move is legal, but because there is an invisible enemy unit, the actual consequences will differ from the preview. Making the process for how this is resolved visually clear will be important to explain to the player why the actual results differ from what the preview said they should expect after they made that move.

A combination of showing a unit moving one tile at a time, combined with popups saying things like "AMBUSH!" or "OVERWATCH" may help visually communicate what is happening at each step in the resolution rather than jumping directly to an end state that does not actually match what the preview showed the player to expect.

Also, and this is perhaps a different topic, it's probably a good idea to have clearly enumerated vision rules and detection rules, in a game where imperfect information is a factor. Looking at this map it isn't really clear to me where units can see and can't see, or where an invisible unit *could* be. For example, showing Fog of War, or having a rule to the effect of "invisible units can be detected at range X." In a tile-based game adjacency is probably the smallest sensible detection range, because at a distance of zero you have already had a collision, and it does not look like this tile implementation allows multiple-occupant tiles. Adjacent tiles is literally as close as it is possible to be to another entity in this map. So it might be a good idea to consider having units detect invisible enemies that are literally in adjacent tiles at minimum, with an ambush occurring if you make a move forward and run into an enemy in a tile further away than an adjacent tile. Other units might have better detection ranges than adjacent (1 tile range), but because a collision is being resolved now without entering the same tile, a unit should probably always be guaranteed to detect any enemy on an adjacent tile.

replies.author: Kingfish344
replies.body: Man, really appreciate your advice here. Units can occupy the same space, but I generally try and avoid. So, flying units are not allowed to be over a ground unit directly. My only real exception is the buried unit, because it is hidden. But once it attacks it becomes surfaced and cannot continue to occupy the same space. Still working on the mechanics of this and your advice is helpful here as well. I also like the idea of a pop up saying ambush/overwatch. I do think stopping the unit at that point would be key here. Vision isn't fully built yet and fog of war is a real thing for this game. And you are correct, a buried hidden unit purposely allows for a move that isn't really allowed because you are going to be ambushed but the user doesn't know that yet so path is found and later discovers it isn't really. Overwatch, could be shown in route though so that visually should be made. I can have it optionally route around the overwatch in that scenario if possible.

replies.author: caster
replies.body:
Definitely need to nail down exactly the rules for how this works. One way this might go could be:

1. A unit moving may not end its move in the same tile occupied by another unit.

2. A unit moving may not move through a tile occupied by an enemy unit.

3. If a unit attempts to move into a tile containing a hidden enemy unit, their move immediately terminates, and the unit is Ambushed. (and explain how Ambush works, damage, etc.)

4. Flying units are exempt from being Ambushed and may move over tiles occupied by enemy units.

5. A unit moving into a tile that is being Overwatched by an enemy unit will have its move terminated and the unit is Overwatched (and detail how Overwatch works)

6. Hidden units are exempt from Overwatch and may move over tiles that are being Overwatched.

replies.author: Kingfish344
replies.body:
And I have mostly already done this. The problem is more to do with the actual ambush itself that is unresolved.   
1. already done (except for underground)  
2. Already done   
3. This is done, but needs some work. Note, ambush is a state and if not in ambushing state they will not be ambushed.  
4. Already done  
5. Agreed need to work on this some as should show in pre view as you mentioned earlier  
6. Already done

I have layering as it's on class with three layers. One rule is no unit can be in same tile as another unit in same layer. However, I could have two units in same tile in different layers, but have only chosen to allow this for hidden units. Main reason that I took an avoidance approach instead of a hard rule is because buried units are naturally hidden but generally having two units in the same spot doesn't look good visually.   
Based on the rule above, the ambushed unit upon being ambushed they both become layered as surfaced and cannot coexist in the same tile anymore so one has to move. That is the part I am struggling to make clean based on the discussion.  
Another rule worth mentioning and why I need a clean rule here. I purposely am making every decision deterministic, no randomness. So, I need a clear rule on what and how a unit moves when being ambushed. But I think I have a solution now.

replies.author: caster
replies.body: I think the most intuitive solution is to check if the unit can move from one tile into the next tile, and if that tile is occupied by a hidden enemy unit, then it can't move. Instead it stops its movement right there and is Ambushed. This prevents needing to put the two units in the same tile at all.

comments.author: Inner-Core-Studios
comments.body: So that menu is basically what people are complaining about regarding Ai Slop. I would strongly advice against using such images in any way. What helps is to tell Ai to make the images vectorized and then make them into png or jpeg sprites for your game. This makes the game already look much less Ai like. I hope you take this as constructive feedback.

replies.author: Kingfish344
replies.body: Totally appreciate it and have realized that was the biggest critique. I already plan on replacing the image as soon as possible. To me the background image was totally unimportant and is the thing I got most burned on. Oh well, live and learn :)

replies.author: Inner-Core-Studios
replies.body: I understand, my comment was not only against the background actually, because I know from experience that in game assets also can look extremely bad when you just ask Ai to make X game asset. But when you tell it, make it a vector image first, that already looks so much better and something a human could have made. Try it. And thanks for being understanding

replies.author: Kingfish344
replies.body:
So what is the prompt to get better art. I spent all this time making art, but if I need to start over, so be it. All the image sprites were done with ChatGPT.  
"let's redo all the unit and structure idle images but build them with a vector" Basically kind of basic but is that the right prompt?

replies.author: Inner-Core-Studios
replies.body:
Yes you could try, but dont let it implement it yet, I would say: I want you to redo all the units and structure images, but dont put them in the game yet. I first want to review them. If you have animations, let it know that. For example you have a tank. I dont know if its supposed to rotate the thing on top, otherwise tell it to make the tank into 2 parts so it can rotate and make for the image also an integration document.

I'm not saying this is perfect or that I'm an expert, but I found that this direction works better at least for me. Good luck!
